content: The text provided appears to be a list of references formatted in a fragmented and non-standard way. It includes citations for various studies, reports, and guidelines related to public health, adolescent health, substance use, physical activity, nutrition, violence prevention, and other topics. 1. Hanson KL, Medina KL, Padula CB, Tapert SF, and Brown SA conducted a study examining the long-term effects of adolescent alcohol and drug use on neuropsychological functioning in young adulthood. Their findings, based on a 10-year follow-up, were published in the Journal of Child and Adolescent Substance Abuse in 2011 (Volume 20, Pages 135–154). 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) released the Global Status Report on Alcohol and Health 2018, which provides comprehensive data on alcohol consumption and its health impacts worldwide. 3. WHO maintains a data portal on maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health, including indicators such as the proportion of students who have ever used marijuana. This resource was last accessed on June 26, 2023. 4. A WHO webpage on cannabis provides information on its use, effects, and related public health concerns. This page was last accessed on September 10, 2022. 5. Ma C, Xi B, Li Z, Wu H, Zhao M, Liang Y, and colleagues analyzed the prevalence and trends of tobacco use among adolescents aged 13–15 years across 143 countries from 1999 to 2018. Their findings were published in The Lancet Child & Adolescent Health in 2021 (Volume 5, Pages 245–255). 6. Kim J, Lee S, and Chun J conducted an international systematic review on the prevalence, risk factors, and protective factors associated with e-cigarette use among young people. Their study was published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health in 2022 (Volume 19, Article 11570). 7. WHO published guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behavior, emphasizing the importance of regular physical activity for health. These guidelines were last accessed on May 6, 2023. 8. Guthold R, Stevens GA, Riley LM, and Bull FC conducted a pooled analysis of 298 population-based surveys involving 1.6 million participants to examine global trends in insufficient physical activity among adolescents. Their study was published in The Lancet Child & Adolescent Health in 2020 (Volume 4, Pages 23–35). 9. Van Sluijs EMF, Ekelund U, Crochemore-Silva I, Guthold R, Ha A, Lubans D, and colleagues reviewed current evidence on physical activity behaviors in adolescence and identified opportunities for intervention. Their findings were published in The Lancet in 2021 (Volume 398, Pages 429–442). 10. Fairclough SJ explored the potential health and well-being concerns associated with adolescents' digital screen time. This work was last accessed on May 6, 2023. 11. Saunders TJ and Vallance JK reviewed the relationship between screen time and health indicators among children and youth, highlighting current evidence, limitations, and future research directions. Their study was published in Applied Health Economics and Health Policy in 2017 (Volume 15, Pages 323–331). 12. Cao K, Wan Y, Yusufu M, and Wang N conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to assess the significance of outdoor time in preventing myopia. Their findings were published in Ophthalmic Research in 2020 (Volume 63, Pages 97–105). 13. WHO's Global Accelerated Action for the Health of Adolescents (AA-HA.) framework provides a comprehensive strategy for improving adolescent health outcomes. 14. WHO published a guideline on effective actions to improve adolescent nutrition, addressing key issues and challenges in the health sector. This document was last accessed on May 6, 2023. 15. WHO provides resources on noncommunicable diseases, including information on childhood overweight and obesity, which was last accessed on September 17, 2022. 16. A pooled analysis of 2,181 population-based studies involving 65 million participants examined height and body mass index trajectories of school-aged children and adolescents from 1985 to 2019 across 200 countries and territories. The findings were published in The Lancet in 2020 (Volume 396, Pages 1511–1524). 17. Maiano C, Hue O, Morin AJ, and Moullec G conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the prevalence of overweight and obesity among children and adolescents with intellectual disabilities. Their study was published in Obesity Reviews in 2016 (Volume 17, Pages 599–611). 18. WHO released a guideline on implementing effective actions to improve adolescent nutrition, which was last accessed on May 6, 2023. 19. Singh N, De Jong J, Popple K, Undie C-C, El Masri R, Bakesiima R, and colleagues emphasized the need to invest in adolescent well-being in humanitarian and fragile settings. Their background paper was last accessed on June 15, 2023. 20. WHO's Global Strategy for Every Woman Every Child in Every Setting outlines a comprehensive approach to improving health outcomes for women and children. 21. Bendavid E, Boerma T, Akseer N, Langer A, Malembaka EB, Okiro EA, and colleagues examined the effects of armed conflict on the health of women and children. Their findings were published in The Lancet in 2021 (Volume 397, Pages 522–532). 22. WHO's Inter-Agency Field Manual on Reproductive Health in Humanitarian Settings provides guidance for addressing reproductive health needs in crisis situations. 23. WHO published an operational guide on child and adolescent health in humanitarian settings, emphasizing a holistic approach for program managers. This document was last accessed on August 7, 2023. 24. Save the Children published a report titled Too Young to Wed: The Growing Problem of Child Marriage Among Syrian Girls in Jordan, highlighting the issue of child marriage in humanitarian contexts. 25. WHO's World Report on Violence and Health provides a comprehensive overview of violence as a public health issue. This report was last accessed on May 6, 2023.
